title: Respect gateway allocations in DB computer

timeline.message:
Respect gateway allocations in DB computer

If one of the gateway allocators initializes a shard somewhere then the
spawned desired balance computation should start from a state with that
shard initializing. Today it doesn't, but this commit fixes that.

Closes #91451
Closes #91613
timeline.author: David Turner

timeline.message: Drop gateway allocations early for legacy allocator
timeline.author: David Turner
David Turner

timeline.body: NIT: consider renaming to `getAndResetGatewayAllocations()` otherwise it looks like this is not doing anything

It is very confusing that getter call also stops tracking something.
Should there be a dedicated call instead? 

Or may be even explicit method to start tracking instead of listing places that do not need to.
It is very easy to miss a new exception as everything would keep working as is, otherwise if we forget to opt in then something would not work.

reply.body: Yeah I don't like this and it's causing many test failures. Better approach incoming.

timeline.message: Be explicit about scope of allocation tracking
timeline.author: David Turner

timeline.message: Different approach: just rebuild the routing table
timeline.author: David Turner

timeline.body: Unfortunately that didn't work because the `ReplicaShardAllocator` also sometimes fails an `INITIALIZING` shard to cancel a recovery in favour of a more efficient recovery elsewhere. Tracking all these changes individually seems too complicated now, so I've opted for just rebuilding the routing table if needed.
